question.problem:
$$ \{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=x(t)+y(t) \\ {y}^{′}(t)=y(t),\end{aligned}\,[\begin{aligned}x(4) \\ y(4)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] $$ Find the solution to the initial value problem above. *Hint: ${e}^{At}=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} & t{e}^{t} \\ 0 & {e}^{t}\end{aligned}],$ where $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}].$*
$[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}]=\,\,$ {{field-1}}
{{field-2}}
question.worked_solution:
Writing our system in matrix form, we get

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]x(t),
$$

where $x(t)=[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}].$ So, the matrix of the system is $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}].$

Given the system ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t),$ where $A$ is a constant square matrix, the general solution of the system can be written as

$$
x(t)=Φ(t)\,c,
$$

where $Φ(t)$ is a fundamental matrix of the system, and $c$ is a constant vector.

So, we can write our general solution as

$$
x(t)={Φ}_{0}(t)c={e}^{At}\,c,
$$

where ${Φ}_{0}(t)={e}^{At}$ is the standard fundamental matrix of the system. Substituting $t={t}_{0},$ we have

$$
x({t}_{0})={e}^{A{t}_{0}}\,c,
$$

and since ${e}^{At}$ is invertible for all $t,$ we have

$$
c={e}^{-A{t}_{0}}\,x({t}_{0}).
$$

Plugging the above back into our expression for $x(t),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & ={e}^{At}\,{e}^{-A{t}_{0}}\,x({t}_{0}) \\  & ={e}^{A(t-{t}_{0})}\,x({t}_{0}).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & ={e}^{A(t-4)}\,x(4) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{t-4} & (t-4){e}^{t-4} \\ 0 & {e}^{t-4}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\,(5-t){e}^{t-4}\, \\ \,-{e}^{t-4}\,\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
